Both mark the end of pallor by the chariot's arrival (பொலந்தேர்க் கொண்கன் வந்தனன் ... நகுக / பொன்னம் பசலையும் தீர்ந்தது ... தேர் இதோ), a stock situation. The same sleepless camp is a separation grief in one and a royal virtue in the other, a specific pairing.

The Kural's honesty does not assume open roads; the link is the shared topic of trade dressed up as a dependency.

The rewarded bard meeting a hungry one is in both (நின்னினும் புல்லியேம் மன்னே in Puram 141; பழம்பசி கூர்ந்தவெம் மிரும்பே ரொக்கலொடு ... வருதும் in the idyll), and Puram 141's thurai is itself பாணாற்றுப்படை. What they share is the genre's frame; that the long poem 'grew' from the short one is assumed rather than shown.

Both lay restraint on the asker: பிச்சைபுக் குண்பான் பிளிறாமை and இரப்பான் வெகுளாமை. The agreement is real, but both are didactic books of the same group and the teaches says only that the needy too have a duty, which each verse already shows alone.

Kural 1321 grants the man no fault (இல்லை தவறவர்க்கு) and yet the sulk; Paripadal 12 shows a man who has eyed another's breasts (பூண் ஆரம் நோக்கிப் புணர் முலை பார்த்தான்), then பிழை ஒன்றும் காணான் தொழுது பிழை கேட்கும், which the onlookers mock as தூயவனைக் காண்மின். Two different poets' heroines speak of the நட்பு with the shore lord: 313 as யாத்தன்று ... அவிழ்த்தற் கரிது, 304 as பகைதரு நட்பு. The contrast is real, but the teaches makes them one bond in one story, so that 313's knot explains 304's grief; that sequence is the linker's construction.

Both grow love-sickness as a plant fed or formed by gossip: ஊரவர் கெளவை எருவாக against ஊரோர் எடுத்த அம்பல் அம்சினை ... அலர்அரும்பு. The contrast between gossip as manure and gossip as branch and bud is good, but calling the couplet 'the seed' of Avvaiyar's tree asserts a direction of borrowing the texts do not show and that runs against the usual order of the two books.

The same battlefield-sacrifice figure is in both: தொடித்தோள் துடுப்பின் துழந்த வல்சி in Puram 26 and தொடித் தோட்கை துடுப் பாக ஆடுற்ற ஊன் சோறு in the idyll, for the same Pandya. Puram 26 sets it beside the Vedic வேள்வி முற்றிய, and the idyll names பிற் பெயராப் படையோர்க்கு, so each adds what the other lacks. That the poet is the same rests on the colophon.

Both look at the reaped millet stubble (இருவை நீள்புனம் / கோல் தலை இருவி). Natrinai 306 asks how he will come to the bare field now the girl is sent home; Ainkurunuru 284's parrots பிரிதல் தேற்றாப் பேரன் பினவே even at the stubble. The pair shows a love that outlasts the field's reason for meeting, with marriage the only way left, a specific reading both texts support.

Kural 1099 makes ஏதிலார் போலப் பொதுநோக்கு a sign found only in lovers, read from outside; Natrinai 75's rejected man is wounded by her உறாஅ நோக்கம் like a hunter's arrow. The same unlooking glance read as disguise by an observer and as refusal by the man is a specific contrast.

Both are by Ammuvanar on rebirth: Kuruntokai 49 prays இம்மை மாறி மறுமை யாயினும் நீயா கியரென் கணவனை, Natrinai 397 fears பிறப்புப் பிறிது ஆகுவதுஆயின் மறக்குவேன்கொல் என் காதலன். Hope and fear about the same belief, both measured by the present love, is accurate and specific.

Kural 719 is a rule of knowing the assembly (புல்லவையுள் பொச்சாந்தும் சொல்லற்க); Pazhamozhi 15 says speaking finely among the unlearned is the worst thing for a man and backs it with the proverb இழுக்கத்தின் மிக்க இழிவில்லை ... ஒழுக்கத்தின் மிக்க உயர்வு. Reclassing the fault as a lapse of conduct is a real extension.

Kuruntokai 32 says that if one can tell the hours apart (பொழுதிடை தெரியின்) love is false, meaning there is no hour without pain; Natrinai 152 gives pain to each hour (புலம்பு தந்தன்றே ... கங்குலும் கையறவு தந்தன்று), which agrees that every hour hurts. The conflict depends on taking தெரிதல் as merely naming hours. Both are madal poems, a closer link the note leaves out.

This is a puram name in an akam simile: the heron's cry sounds like the chariots bards won at ஆஅய் வண் மகிழ் நாளவை, and Puram 127 shows Ay's hall emptied by bards. The note says what the akam poet does with it, setting the bard who goes home rich against the go-between turned away (பை தீர் பாண ... பணி மொழி களையா).

Both are the foster mother's search after the elopement, treated differently: Akananuru 7 still questions a hill girl (நின்னொடு வினவல் கேளாய்), and Kuruntokai 44 has worn legs, eyes that வாளிழந்தன and others more than the stars. The contrast is fair, but setting them as 'middle' and 'end' of one search is the linker's sequence, and Kuruntokai 44's link to the search rests on its thurai.

Thirumurugatruppadai 6 names only மறுவில் கற்பின் வாணுதற் கணவன்; Paripadal 9 names the bride as the daughter of the thousand-eyed one, married at பரங்குன்று. Identifying the two is reasonable, but the teaches' claim that this 'explains why' Parankunram is the guide poem's first abode is not in either text.

Both hang a weight from life with the verb தூங்கு: சிறுகோட்டுப் பெரும்பழந் தூங்கி யாங்கிவள் உயிர்தவச் சிறிது காமமோ பெரிதே, and காமமும் நாணும் உயிர்காவாத் தூங்கும். The Kural's added counterweight of shame, turning the stalk into a carrying pole, is a specific change the pair shows.

poems.note: The rain is addressed as pitiless in the poem's own statement, so it carries the stated sense rather than raising another.

iraicchi.act: the stags play everywhere with their does while the fawns leap
iraicchi.sense: in the season he named the creatures keep their mates, so his staying away is a broken promise and she has spent her life for nothing

poems.note: The stripped omai and the calling dove map well onto the deserted heroine, but she is the speaker and the wasteland road is not something she knows.

iraicchi.act: the soft-gaited wild cow sleeps secure on the leaf-sheltered cool slope
iraicchi.sense: as the creature rests safe in the slope's shelter, the girl can rest only in the man's protection, so he must keep her

poems.note: The punnai's buds opening, flowers taken for garlands and fruit hanging map onto the love moving to its fruit in marriage, which the thurai and line 6 state.
Colophon gives vaakai (puram), so both fields are null.

iraicchi.act: the boar grazes the guarded millet and then sleeps without fear on the rock slope
iraicchi.sense: the boar raids the guarded field and rests unafraid, so the man's staying away for fear of the father has no excuse

poems.note: The backwater is made a woman openly (முகமா, கண் ஆக), an open comparison.

iraicchi.act: the bees hum in every grove with the mates they love
iraicchi.sense: every creature is with its mate while she lies sleepless alone

poems.note: The contrast is spoken in the poem's list (யானே ...), so the sense is close to stated.
The bull-fight similes are open comparisons (போல், போன்ம்).
Herons bringing fish smell to the jackfruit tree and the young monkey unable to bear it map onto the visits that raise talk and the girl's distress; the mapping is not certain.
The fisher girl's basket of fish and the wife filling it with paddy map onto the courtesan's trade and the household's wealth spent on it; the second pair is open to dispute.

iraicchi.act: the dove sulks with its cock
iraicchi.sense: sulking with a present mate is waste, since a parted lover leaves only pallor

poems.note: The moral is spoken to the dove, so the sense is near stated.
